pages.title: Thermal Heater
pages.text: A fuel-burning heater. Right-click with coal, charcoal, blaze powder, coal blocks or cryo fuel to refuel. Inside a sealed room it heats the air, then the walls and floor. Open camps retain nearby warmth.$(br2)$(l:heating/heater_upgrades)Upgrades$(/l) add power. Larger rooms warm more slowly. $(l:heating/room_climate)Room Heating & Insulation$(/l) explains building and fuel use.
Surround a Thermal Core with 8 iron ingots. It's essentially an iron box with a hot thing inside. ORSA charged the UN four billion credits for this design.

pages.title: Automatic Control
pages.text: Heaters share a 20°C room target and throttle as the room warms. Connected Core and fire heat contributes to that same temperature. Extra heaters speed warm-up; they do not raise the target.$(br2)Redstone stops heating and holds ordinary fuel use. Stored heat cools naturally.$(br2)An $(l:heating/thermostat)ORSA Thermostat$(/l) sets 10-30°C for every linked heater.

pages.title: Fuel and Companionship
pages.text: The status panel shows Heating or Holding, burn percentage and estimated fuel time. Better insulation reduces holding demand. Frostmites and machinery can add separate fuel costs.$(br2)$(italic)ORSA FAQ: “Can I name the heater?” We cannot stop you. Please seek companionship elsewhere.$()

pages.title: Airless Rooms
pages.text: With no air, heaters and passive sources deliver reduced heat to the walls. Heater wall heating stops at its room target; passive sources cannot heat a reservoir above their supply temperature. Refilling cannot create heat.$(br2)Vacuum can still feel cold while walls are warm. A heater does not replace EVA. Unknown or unloaded room geometry suspends heating without restoring local source bonuses.$(br2)Already-hot walls cool naturally or through a heat vent; resealing does not reset them.
